title: A&O Shearman and Harvey to Roll Out Agentic AI Agents Targeting Complex Legal Workflows
author: A&O Shearman

dom.t: Vertical AI: Commercial traction cannot prove defensibility

st.t: Power users: Usage volume may obscure value
st.an: The source accepts the proposition that value comes from embedding AI into redesigned, expertise-led workflows rather than merely providing access. It adds a concrete firm–vendor collaboration around ContractMatrix and agentic workflows, while its claimed time, accuracy and quality gains remain participant endorsements without independent measurement.
qs: In 2023, A&O Shearman became the first firm globally to build an AI app for in-house counsel by collaborating with Harvey and Microsoft to create ContractMatrix, an AI-powered contract tool.
Together with A&O Shearman, Harvey is building agentic workflows that save tremendous amounts of time without sacrificing accuracy and trust.

st.t: Vertical AI: Commercial traction cannot prove defensibility
st.an: The announcement supports the cluster’s account of vertical legal AI moving into embedded, multi-step workflows and software-enabled service models. Its claims of faster, better work are promotional and unquantified, so it provides no evidence that operational promise or commercialisation establishes durable defensibility.
qs: These AI agents incorporate expertise from A&O Shearman's leading practices into agentic systems that can conduct research and engage in multi-step reasoning over matter-specific documents and curated data.
Available to large corporations, law firms, and financial services via subscription or usage-based fees, A&O Shearman will share in the software revenue.

kp.k: Firm and vendor launch legal AI agents
kp.d: A&O Shearman announces that it and Harvey are launching agentic AI systems for complex legal tasks. The systems are intended for internal deployment and external sale to corporate clients, financial-services businesses and other law firms.
qs: A&O Shearman and Harvey are launching a series of agentic, multi-step reasoning AI agents for complex legal tasks.
The agents integrate A&O Shearman’s legal expertise and will be rolled out internally as well as being sold to clients and other law firms.

kp.k: Initial agents target four high-value practice areas
kp.d: The first agents address antitrust filing analysis, cybersecurity, fund formation and loan review, which the source characterises as high-value fields involving deep expertise and multi-step reasoning.
qs: The initial agents focus on antitrust filing analysis, cybersecurity, fund formation, and loan review—high-value areas requiring deep legal expertise and multi-step reasoning.

kp.k: Agents decompose and execute complex legal workflows
kp.d: The announced systems combine matter-specific documents, curated data and A&O Shearman practice expertise. They are described as researching issues, forming actionable plans, completing interdependent steps and assembling intermediate results into complete work products, subject to transparency and oversight.
qs: These AI agents incorporate expertise from A&O Shearman's leading practices into agentic systems that can conduct research and engage in multi-step reasoning over matter-specific documents and curated data.
These agents break down complex issues into actionable plans, finish them interdependently, and combine intermediate outputs into complete work products with transparency and oversight.

kp.k: Law firm will share software revenue
kp.d: The offering extends A&O Shearman’s business beyond delivering legal work into sharing revenue from software supplied through subscriptions or usage-based charges. The stated customers include large corporations, law firms and financial-services organisations.
qs: Available to large corporations, law firms, and financial services via subscription or usage-based fees, A&O Shearman will share in the software revenue.

kp.k: Partner claims tasks fall from hours to minutes
kp.d: David Wakeling characterises the agents as the first concrete legal applications of agentic AI within a multinational law firm and claims they reduce work previously requiring several hours to minutes. The announcement provides no benchmark, sample size or methodology supporting that performance claim.
qs: There has been a lot of hype, but these agents are the first concrete legal use-cases of agentic AI within a multinational law firm—and therefore within much of the commercial landscape.
These agents do in minutes what previously took several hours, and frustrated people.

kp.k: Harvey predicts time savings without reduced trust
kp.d: Harvey co-founder Winston Weinberg argues that the collaboration challenges the legal industry’s longstanding delivery structure. He claims the workflows can produce substantial time savings without compromising accuracy or trust and predicts significant potential for the industry and clients.
qs: For decades, the legal industry has relied on the same structure and approach to deliver results for clients.
Together with A&O Shearman, Harvey is building agentic workflows that save tremendous amounts of time without sacrificing accuracy and trust.
This combination presents a powerful combination with remarkable potential for the industry and for current and future clients.

kp.k: Antitrust partner says work is improving
kp.d: A&O Shearman antitrust partner James Webber presents the technology as a response to slow and difficult antitrust work. His comments predict that burdensome manual approaches are receding and assert that resulting work is getting better, without supplying quantitative evidence.
qs: All lawyers working on antitrust matters have had that sinking feeling – usually around 3am – of ‘there must be an easier and quicker way of doing this’.
Those days are fading fast. The work is getting better.

kp.k: Loan agent reviews and compares agreement portfolios
kp.d: Leveraged-finance partner Filippo Crosara says manual loan-document review is time-intensive and requires experience and sophisticated skills. He describes an agent that reviews loan agreements, extracts data and conducts comparative portfolio analysis, and predicts that it will improve the firm’s client offering.
qs: Loan documentation for leveraged finance transactions is highly complex and bespoke, while manual review is time intensive, requiring experience and a sophisticated skillset.
In partnership with Harvey, we’ve created an agent that is able to review loan agreements, extract data and perform comparative analysis across portfolios—quickly, reliably and efficiently.
This exciting innovation will enhance A&O Shearman’s ability to provide the most advanced solutions to our clients.

kp.k: Launch follows earlier firmwide AI deployments
kp.d: The source situates the agents within a longer adoption timeline, claiming that the firm deployed generative AI enterprise-wide in 2022 and collaborated with Harvey and Microsoft in 2023 to create ContractMatrix, an AI-powered contract tool for in-house counsel.
qs: In 2022, A&O Shearman became the first firm to deploy generative AI enterprise-wide.
In 2023, A&O Shearman became the first firm globally to build an AI app for in-house counsel by collaborating with Harvey and Microsoft to create ContractMatrix, an AI-powered contract tool.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: A&O Shearman announces agents that perform multi-step work in complex legal practice areas and turn intermediate results into complete work products.
pts.d: The firm describes agents combining its legal expertise with Harvey's technology to research matter-specific documents and curated data, decompose issues into plans, and complete interdependent tasks with transparency and oversight. Initial applications are antitrust filing analysis, cybersecurity, fund formation, and loan review. This is a claim about automating complex workflows, not an explicit claim that lawyers can be removed from the process.

pts.k: The firm plans to commercialise its embedded legal expertise through software fees, alongside internal deployment.
pts.d: A&O Shearman says the agents will be sold to clients and other law firms through subscription or usage-based pricing, with the firm sharing software revenue. The announcement therefore identifies a software-revenue channel for a law firm; it does not say that this replaces hourly billing or existing legal services.

pts.k: David Wakeling claims hours-to-minutes time savings and describes the agents as the first concrete legal applications of agentic AI within a multinational law firm.
pts.d: Wakeling, A&O Shearman's Global Head of AI Advisory and the Markets Innovation Group, presents these as current capabilities. He associates the time savings with relief from frustrating work. His priority claim and performance claim are attributed statements rather than independently established findings in the document.

pts.k: Harvey CEO Winston Weinberg claims major time savings without loss of accuracy or trust; James Webber claims antitrust work is improving.
pts.d: Weinberg characterises the collaboration as a departure from longstanding legal delivery structures and predicts broader potential for the industry and clients. Webber, an A&O Shearman antitrust partner, says burdensome late-night work is receding and work quality is improving. Neither specifies a measured accuracy or quality outcome.

pts.k: Filippo Crosara claims the loan-review agent can quickly and reliably review bespoke agreements, extract data, and compare portfolios.
pts.d: Crosara, an A&O Shearman leveraged finance partner, contrasts the agent's capabilities with manual review requiring substantial time, experience, and sophisticated skills. He presents the agent as already created and predicts that it will enhance the firm's client services.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered consists of product descriptions, participant testimony, professional experience, and the firm's prior AI deployments.
pts.d: This firm-news announcement relies on statements by participating partners and Harvey's CEO. Crosara explicitly invokes more than two decades of leveraged finance experience. The firm cites its enterprise-wide generative AI deployment in 2022 and its 2023 ContractMatrix collaboration with Harvey and Microsoft as implementation background. No benchmark, sample size, testing protocol, independent evaluation, measured error rate, or documented client outcome is supplied for the time, accuracy, reliability, or quality claims.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: As of April 6, 2025, the source describes an ongoing launch, existing agent capabilities, and prospective internal and commercial rollout without a completion date.
pts.d: Present-tense statements describe the agents as capable of performing work now, while future-tense statements concern deployment, sales, revenue sharing, and improved client services. Initial scope is limited to the four named practice applications. The described operating context includes matter-specific documents, curated data, embedded legal expertise, transparency, and oversight; the source gives no detailed supervision or verification protocol.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The announced effects concern commercial legal practitioners, corporate and financial-services buyers, other law firms, and A&O Shearman as a software-revenue participant.
pts.d: Lawyers in the initial practice areas are expected to spend less time on complex research and review, with antitrust and leveraged finance partners highlighting reduced burdens and improved work. Large corporations, financial-services organisations, and other law firms are prospective paying users. A&O Shearman expects both internal service-delivery benefits and a share of software revenue. The source makes no concrete prediction about staffing reductions, junior recruitment, client fee reductions, or access to justice.
